concepts.name: Cartesian Coordinate System
concepts.description: The Cartesian coordinate system uses two perpendicular number lines, called the x-axis and y-axis, to locate points on a plane. Every point is represented by an ordered pair of coordinates.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify and plot points on the Cartesian plane using ordered pairs.

concepts.name: Coordinates and Quadrants
concepts.description: The coordinate plane is divided into four quadrants based on the signs of the x- and y-coordinates. Understanding quadrants helps determine the position of points accurately.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to identify the quadrant in which a given point lies.

concepts.name: Distance Between Two Points
concepts.description: The distance formula calculates the length of the line segment joining two points in the coordinate plane using the Pythagorean Theorem.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the distance between two points using the distance formula.

concepts.name: Derivation of the Distance Formula
concepts.description: The distance formula is derived by constructing a right triangle between two points and applying the Pythagorean Theorem.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to explain the derivation of the distance formula.

concepts.name: Applications of the Distance Formula
concepts.description: The distance formula is used to determine lengths, verify geometric properties, and solve practical coordinate geometry problems.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply the distance formula to solve geometric and real-life problems.

concepts.name: Internal Division of a Line Segment
concepts.description: The section formula determines the coordinates of a point that divides a line segment internally in a given ratio.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to find the coordinates of a point dividing a line segment internally in a specified ratio.

concepts.name: Midpoint Formula
concepts.description: The midpoint formula is a special case of the section formula where the ratio is 1:1. It gives the coordinates of the midpoint of a line segment.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to calculate the midpoint of a line segment using the midpoint formula.

concepts.name: Applications of the Section Formula
concepts.description: The section formula is useful in geometry, construction, navigation, and graphical representation of proportional divisions.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to solve coordinate geometry problems involving proportional division of line segments.

concepts.name: Key Concepts of Coordinate Geometry
concepts.description: This chapter summarizes the Cartesian coordinate system, distance formula, section formula, and midpoint formula, which are fundamental tools for solving geometric problems analytically.
concepts.learning_outcome: Students will be able to apply coordinate geometry formulas to determine distances, midpoints, and points of division in the Cartesian plane.
